prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital medication dispensing/returns, clinical control/accountability. Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer.
Morrowglass timestamps/validates authorized orders, flags omissions/duplicates/conflicts, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot, routes review, reports status. Clinical Pharmacist approves appropriateness/dose/allergy/interaction checks, resolves clinical questions, produces Dose Exception Review Slip, assesses storage/timing-compromised medication suitability. Copperfield investigates/escalates discrepancies, verifies identity/packaging/lot/expiry/handling, prepares medication, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card; rechecks delayed capsule contents/order identifiers before retry. Cinderwake prepares reviewed/authorized active orders, records handling, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Juniper supports final verification/auditable decisions. Unresolved discrepancies block preparation; incomplete checks/unauthorized status block dispensing.
Bluejay continuously monitors approved temperatures, timestamps readings, reports excursions/connectivity loss; retain duration/extent records, segregate affected stock pending authorized disposition. Tallowmere records returns, produces Return Bin Audit Label per transaction; segregate pending assessment. Medication Safety Officer oversees safety/trends/procedures, produces Diversion Review Packet.
East Tube Dispatch Console/West Tube Dispatch Console control authorized routing; Pneumatic Tube Network transports compatible deliveries; Hospital Courier handles unsuitable/unavailable automation. East records capsule route/timing/equipment status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket for route/interval failures. Dispatch personnel hold affected capsules/block faulted routes. Operations staff review queues, coordinate approved alternates with wards; resume only after safety testing/required checks/operations authorization.
Larkspur confirms continuing need/follows delay contingency. Charge Nurse coordinates readiness/escalation, communicates delays/workarounds, sends Cabinet Downtime Notice, confirms notification before restoration. North Ward Cabinet Controller/South Ward Cabinet Controller report availability/block dispensing in Out of Service state. Ward contingency requires authorized dispensing/access/cabinet controls/accountability.
Stonewake supports recovery, inspects tube hardware/switches/sensors, checks repaired cabinets. IT Operations Specialist checks connectivity/interfaces/applications/logs. Responsible technical staff document faults/corrections/verification in service records.

New part:
S072: A cabinet remains unavailable until its controller reports Ready for Dispense and required operational checks are complete.
S073: Operations closes the interruption only after staff confirm that dispensing and delivery workflows are functioning as intended.
S074: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
S075: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
S076: The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
S077: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
S078: The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
S079: The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
S080: The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
S081: The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
S082: A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
S083: The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
S084: Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
S085: The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
S086: Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
S087: Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
S088: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
S089: At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
S090: The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
S091: The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
S092: The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
S093: The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
S094: The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
